question.problem:
The daily commute time for employees is normally distributed with an average of $40$ minutes and an unknown standard deviation. Tests show that $15%$ of commutes take more than $52$ minutes. Assuming a normal model, what percentage of commutes take less than $31.7$ minutes? **Round the answer to $1$ decimal place.**

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $\,p\,$ | $0.75$ | $0.80$ | $0.85$ | $0.90$ | $0.95$ | $0.97$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ | $\,1.8808\,$ |

*In addition, you're given the following table of values for $p=Φ(z).$*

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.7\,$ | $\,0.2358\,$ | $\,0.2327\,$ | $\,0.2296\,$ |
| $\,-0.6\,$ | $\,0.2676\,$ | $\,0.2643\,$ | $\,0.2611\,$ |
| $\,-0.5\,$ | $\,0.3015\,$ | $\,0.2981\,$ | $\,0.2946\,$ |

Approximately
{{field-1}}$%$ of commutes take less than $31.7$ minutes.
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the commute time (in minutes) of a randomly selected person. Then we have $X∼N(40,{\sigma }^{2}),$ and we want to find $P(X<31.7).$ But first, we need to find the standard deviation $\sigma .$ 

We know that $P(X>52)=0.15.$ First, we convert this to a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 52) & =1-P(X>52) \\  & =1-0.15 \\  & =0.85\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 52) & =0.85 \\ P(Z\le \frac{52-40}{\sigma }) & =0.85 \\ Φ(\frac{12}{\sigma }) & =0.85 \\ \frac{12}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.85).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.85)=1.0364.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{12}{\sigma } & =1.0364 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{12}{1.0364} \\ \sigma  & ≈11.5785.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve for $P(X\le 31.7)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 31.7) & =P(Z\le \frac{31.7-40}{11.5785}) \\  & ≈P(Z\le -0.72) \\  & ≈Φ(-0.72) \\  & =0.2358 \\  & ≈23.6%\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, approximately $23.6%$ of commutes take less than $31.7$ minutes.
